newsitem.title: USA: SEC okays Nasdaq move to narrow quote increments.
newsitem.headline: SEC okays Nasdaq move to narrow quote increments.

text.p: Nasdaq said Wednesday it received federal regulatory approval to narrow its minimum stock quotation increments to 1/16 of a dollar or 6.25 cents from 1/8 of a dollar or 12.5 cents.
The Securities and Exchange Commission approval applies to all securities listed on the electronic stock market whose bid price is $10 or more, Nasdaq said in a statement.
The new quoting system is effective for all Nasdaq stocks on June 2, the stock market said. Stocks under $10 are already quoted in increments as small as 1/32 or 3.125 cents.

"We're delighted the SEC moved quickly to approve our proposal to quote in 1/16," said Frank Zarb, chairman, CEO and president of the National Association of Securities Dealers, parent of the Nasdaq stock market.
The NASD first approved the move to narrow the quotation increments for securities last month before sending it to the SEC for federal approval.
The approval follows the introduction of proposed legislation in March that would require the SEC to develop a plan within a year to move stock and options markets away from trading in fractions.
The narrowing "will enhance transparency and price discovery by allowing orders and quotes in smaller increments to be displayed publicly to the market," Zarb said.
NASD is a trade group for the U.S. financial industry and a self-regulatory organization under SEC oversight.
